title: Pool of Siloam Discovery
summary: A Hebrew inscription commemorating the completion of the Siloam Tunnel.
historical_context: One of the clearest surviving Hebrew construction inscriptions from ancient Judah.
ancient_near_east_context: The item belongs to the broader imperial, cultic, and urban world of the ancient Near East and the biblical periods reflected in the dataset.
literary_context: Often discussed in relation to Hezekiah's water works in Jerusalem.
covenantal_significance: Pool of Siloam Discovery helps anchor biblical claims in historical reality while reminding readers that archaeology supports rather than replaces interpretation.
interpretive_notes: The inscription is genuine, but the exact royal attribution is inferred from context rather than named in the text.
Use the item as context for the biblical text, not as a shortcut around it.
